findings.who: A filer who installed qualifying exterior windows or skylights in 2024 as part of reconstructing their home, but whose original use of the reconstructed home began in 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether anything was installed in 2025 and whether exterior windows or skylights were installed; the physical installation was in 2024, so the filer says no.
findings.irs_text: i5695 p. 1, Costs: "costs are treated as being paid when the original installation of the item is completed, or, in the case of costs connected with the reconstruction of your home, when your original use of the reconstructed home begins"
findings.fix: Ask whether the filer had qualifying window/skylight costs treated as paid in 2025, including when original use of a reconstructed home begins in 2025, not only whether physical installation occurred in 2025.

findings.who: A married couple filing jointly where one spouse owned and lived in a separate main home and installed Energy Star Most Efficient windows or skylights there in 2025, while the other spouse answering the question did not.
findings.why_no: The gate says "Exterior windows or skylights were installed" and the parent says "anything was installed ... at a home" without saying "you or your spouse"; the filer reads it as asking only about their own installation or home and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i5695 p. 3, Married taxpayers with more than one home: "If you are filing a joint return, figure your energy efficient home improvement credit as follows. 1. Complete lines 17a through 30 of a separate Form 5695 for each main home."
findings.fix: Use "you or your spouse" and expressly include a spouse's separate main home on a joint return.

findings.who: A condominium owner or tenant-stockholder in a cooperative housing corporation whose association or cooperative paid for qualifying exterior window or skylight replacement and charged the filer a proportionate share.
findings.why_no: The filer reads the gate as asking whether the filer personally installed windows or skylights and says no because the association or cooperative did the installation and the filer only paid an assessment or share.
findings.irs_text: i5695 p. 2, Association or cooperative costs: "you are treated as having paid your proportionate share of any costs of such association or corporation"
findings.fix: State that the gate is met when the filer or spouse paid, directly or through a condominium or cooperative association, for exterior windows or skylights.

findings.who: A filer who installed only one exterior window or one skylight that meets the Energy Star Most Efficient requirements.
findings.why_no: The gate says "Exterior windows or skylights were installed," using plurals; the filer reads that as requiring more than one and truthfully says no to the plural wording.
findings.irs_text: i5695 p. 6, Lines 20a Through 20d: "Enter the QMID and amounts you paid for the four most expensive exterior windows and skylights ... on lines (i) through (iv)"; the line (ii) help says "Zero if there was one."
findings.fix: Say "any exterior window or skylight" rather than the plural "windows or skylights."

findings.who: A filer who installed qualifying Energy Star Most Efficient exterior windows or skylights in 2025 to replace broken or unattractive windows, improve noise, or for appearance, but not with the purpose of saving or making energy.
findings.why_no: The parent gate asks whether anything was installed "to save or make energy"; the filer says no because energy savings was not their purpose, even though the installed windows meet the tax requirements.
findings.irs_text: i5695 p. 2, Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit: "You may be able to take a credit equal to 30% of the sum of: 1. The amount paid or incurred for qualified energy efficiency improvements installed during 2025..."; fs-2025-01 p. 3: exterior windows and skylights "must meet Energy Star most efficient certification requirements"
findings.fix: Remove the subjective "to save or make energy" purpose from the gate; ask whether qualifying windows or skylights were installed and test qualification separately.

findings.who: A filer who personally installed qualifying exterior windows or skylights rather than hiring a contractor.
findings.why_no: The filer reads "were installed" as requiring professional installation and says no because they did it themselves.
findings.irs_text: fs-2025-01 p. 3, Q3: "Can taxpayers claim the credit for qualified property they install themselves? ... A3. Yes."
findings.fix: Add "including self-installation" or ask "installed or had installed."

findings.who: A filer who installed qualifying exterior windows or skylights in a houseboat, mobile home, or manufactured home and does not think of that dwelling as a "home" for this question.
findings.why_no: The gate says "at a home"; the filer reads "home" colloquially as a house and says no even though the IRS treats these dwellings as homes.
findings.irs_text: i5695 p. 1, Home: "A home is where you lived in 2025 and can include a house, houseboat, mobile home, cooperative apartment, condominium, and a manufactured home..."
findings.fix: List the dwelling types included as a home, or add "including a houseboat, mobile home, or manufactured home."

findings.who: A filer who owned and lived in a main home in 2025, installed qualifying Energy Star Most Efficient windows or skylights there, and sold the home before filing the return.
findings.why_no: The filer reads the gate as requiring them to still own or live in the home when they file and answers no even though the windows were installed during 2025 at their then-main home.
findings.irs_text: i5695 p. 3, Qualified energy efficiency improvements: "building envelope components installed on or in your main home that you owned during 2025"; p. 1: "A home is where you lived in 2025"
findings.fix: Ask whether the home was the filer's main home at any time in 2025; a later sale does not disqualify the installation.
